title: Hits in the last five minutes
prompt:
Build a hit counter for a web page that records hits at integer timestamps and reports how many hits happened in the last 300 seconds.

- Implement the class HitCounter with hit(t) and count(t). The driver runHitCounter(ops) is already written: ops is a list like [["hit", 1], ["count", 4]], and it returns one output per op (null/None for "hit", the number for "count").
- count(t) returns the number of recorded hits with timestamp h where t - 300 < h <= t. A hit at exactly t - 300 no longer counts.
- Timestamps are integers from 1 to 10^9 and never decrease from one op to the next. Several hits may share a timestamp.
- Up to 100,000 ops. Aim for O(1) amortised time per op.
hints: Timestamps only move forward. Once a hit is too old for one count, can it ever count again?
Store hit timestamps in a FIFO queue in arrival order.
In count(t), pop from the front while the oldest timestamp is <= t - 300, then return the queue size.

solution.explanation: Because timestamps never decrease, hits arrive in sorted order and leave the window in the same order, so a FIFO queue is enough. count drops every hit at or before t - 300 from the front and returns the queue length. Each hit is added once and removed at most once.

complexity.notes: w is the number of hits inside the window. With millions of hits per second, 300 (second, count) buckets give O(300) space regardless of traffic.

followUps: How would you bound memory if a single second can receive millions of hits?
What changes if hits can arrive slightly out of order (up to 5 seconds late)?
